Smoothed financial information shapes decisions, protects trust, and gives businesses a clear picture of what they need and what they want. That is what drew me to financial accounting and continues to hold my attention: the opportunity to turn complex figures into accurate, trustworthy stories that help organisations make confident decisions. I am originally from India, and I hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university not listed in the major global rankings. My interest in this field has grown through seeing how much value can come from careful reporting, reconciliations, and the careful matching of figures so that financial information is not only accurate, but usable. That connection became especially personal during a family dinner in the middle of year-end reporting, when I explained how balance sheets work using the restaurant bill; the memory still captures why this work matters to me. It has stayed with me because it reflects the satisfaction of making finance understandable and useful to the people around me.

My academic background gave me a structured foundation, and I have completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing the importance of accuracy and follow-through. In one role, I needed to use a technique that was new to me, so I learned it within a couple of months and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another occasion, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put in place a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped work continue more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on before, and I value those moments because they reflect the importance of clear communication and dependable support. I also took on substantial responsibility beyond my formal role on my own initiative and sustained that effort over many months until the work was completed.

What keeps this career personal for me is how naturally it connects with everyday life. During a family dinner, I calculated a budget for a holiday excursion with the aid of the receipts I had prepared, and my family still jokes that I turned the evening into a finance demonstration. Looking ahead, I want to contribute as a Financial Accountant by supporting accurate reporting, supporting compliance, and helping lead teams to reliable financial information.

Few things are more rewarding than watching a child move from uncertainty to understanding, and that transformation is what drew me towards becoming a Primary School Teacher. Inspired by the way great teachers can shape a child’s confidence as much as their academic progress, I chose primary education to help children discover curiosity, resilience, and a genuine love of learning from the very start. I am originally from the Netherlands, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100. Through my studies and professional development, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in turning complex ideas into engaging, age-appropriate lessons that invite participation from children with different learning styles. One of my favourite memories is of a younger family member visiting my classroom and proudly playing “detective” games with me during a school reading event; that moment captured for me how teaching can reach beyond the classroom and become something others feel connected to as well.

In practice, this has meant learning quickly and applying new knowledge in ways that make a practical difference. When I was assigned work in an unfamiliar area, I spent my first months learning its systems, routines, and expectations, and that experience taught me how to absorb new information quickly and apply it in day-to-day work. In another role, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time at the same stage of a routine process, so I introduced a simple adjustment to the process that reduced delays and saved time across the group. Colleagues now sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value being able to talk through practical answers with them. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when required to bring it through to completion. Altogether, these experiences have prepared me to contribute thoughtfully to a primary school community and to help children grow in understanding, confidence, and participation.

During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when needed to carry it through to completion.

What keeps this career personal for me is how often precision is felt in everyday life. One of my favourite family memories is coming home after a busy week in the lab and finding that my younger sibling had turned our kitchen into a “mini lab,” carefully labelling cups of juice like test samples. It reminded me that the tiniest details can influence the quality of a result, and that sense of discovery has confirmed my direction.

Alongside this, I have developed a practical approach to logistics work that fits the way I like to work: balancing multiple priorities, keeping records, communicating clearly, and responding when plans change. I am now looking to bring that approach to a Logistics Coordinator role where I can contribute to reliable operations, keep teams aligned, and support smooth operations across the organisation.
